body:
Here's the latest from the MLB hot stove on the eve of baseball free agency
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:37 am ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The 2026-27 MLB offseason is only four days old and already the hot stove moves and rumors are coming in. Here are our top 50 free agents and top 25 trade candidates, and here are the important offseason dates and deadlines you need to know. Here now are Sunday's hot stove happenings. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Padres decline Pivetta's option 
San Diego's top two starters are now free agents. Two days after Michael King exercised an opt-out clause to become a free agent, the Padres declined their $14 million club option on Nick Pivetta, reports the San Diego Union-Tribune. Had the Padres picked up the option, Pivetta would have held an $18 million player option for 2028. That surely factored into the team's decision. Pivetta, 34 in February, missed roughly five months with a flexor strain this past season. He returned late in the season and pitched reasonably well in six starts spanning September and the postseason. The San Diego Union-Tribune notes the Padres still have concerns about Pivetta's elbow, but could re-sign him to a new contract with a lower salary and/or no player option.San Diego signed Pivetta to what amounted to a two-year, $23 million contact with two players options in February 2025. The flexor strain triggered an injury clause that converted the 2027 player option into a club option. We ranked Pivetta as the offseason's 43rd-best free agent. 

                            
    
                                                
                    
     Orioles decline Robert's option 
As expected, the Orioles have declined their $20 million club option for center fielder Luis Robert Jr., reports ESPN. They will pay him a $2 million buyout, so it was functionally an $18 million decision. Robert suffered a hamstring injury and played only three games with the O's after being claimed off waivers from the Mets in late September. Now 29, Robert again had multiple stints on the injured list this past season. He continued to punish lefties and play solid center field defense when healthy, but injuries have limited him to only 271 of 489 possible regular-season games from 2024-26. We did not rank Robert among our top 50 free agents, though he is an interesting upside play given his age.  Hanwha Eagles to post Si-Hwan Roh The Hanwha Eagles of the Korea Baseball Organization will post star third baseman Si-Hwan Roh for MLB teams this offseason, reports Yonhap News Agency. Roh signed the richest deal in KBO history in February (11 years and $23 million), though as part of the deal, the Eagles agreed to post him this offseason, and Roh agreed to return to the team once his MLB stint is over. 
Roh, 26, has been one of the KBO's best players the last several years. He hit .283/.360/.505 with 29 home runs in 2026, and has averaged 35 home runs per 162 games since 2023. Roh is considered a reliable but unspectacular defender at third, plus he has first base experience as well. This free agent class is very thin at the hot corner. Roh should generate a good deal of interest. KBO players get a 30-day negotiating window once officially posted. If Roh does not sign with an MLB team during the 30-day window, he will return to the Eagles. It's possible that Roh, a right-handed hitter, will eclipse his $23 million guarantee with the Eagles over just a handful of years with an MLB team. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    
                            
    
                                                
                    
     Astros, Rays make minor trade The Astros have acquired Triple-A righty reliever Evan Reifert from the Rays for cash, reports the Tampa Bay Times. Houston is likely to add him to their 40-man roster to protect him from the Rule 5 Draft. The Rays did not have the roster space to do that, so they traded for cash rather than lose him for nothing. Reifert, 27, has an excellent slider and used it to strike out 81 batters in 58 Triple-A innings in 2026. He should spend time in Houston's bullpen next season.

title: Shooting outside stadium after Magic City Classic in Alabama leaves one dead and eight injured - CBS Sports
description: A deadly shooting outside Legion Field in Birmingham marred the annual game betwen rivals Alabama State and Alaba
body:
A deadly shooting outside Legion Field in Birmingham marred the annual game betwen rivals Alabama State and Alabama A&M
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:52 am ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
Police have confirmed one death and at least eight injuries following a mass shooting after Saturday's "Magic City Classic" college football game featuring Alabama A&M and Alabama State at Birmingham's Legion Field.Michael Pickett, chief of the Birmingham Police Department, told media outlets he was "very grateful that more people weren't injured" in the shooting after Alabama A&M's 31-28 win over Alabama State came in front of a near sellout crowd of 70,000-plus fans.The shooting happened just before 8 p.m. local time (CT) near Graymont Avenue West and Fourth Street West just outside Legion Field where vendors and fans were gathered for postgame tailgating. Multiple emergency and police personnel responded to calls after the shooting, according to AL.com.Birmingham police officer De'Rell Freeman said one person had been detained and transported to police headquarters and that multiple weapons were gathered.Pickett categorized the shooting as "two senseless acts of violence" during his brief press conference with local media."This is something that we not only see here in Birmingham, we see it all over the nation," Pickett said, per AL.com. "It's important that we as a community address this issue as a community."Our Birmingham police officers are true heroes. Seeing the courage and the resilience they displayed tonight running alongside them in the direction of those gunshots, that shows the true dedication they have to actually save lives."Birmingham police issued an order for people to leave the area surrounding Legion Field just before 9 p.m. local time.Pickett said Birmingham police would like all video of the incident submitted to them and they're being assisted by the FBI with the case."If you all saw anything, heard anything, recorded something on your device, may have been recording at the time, have any information that could help our investigators, we ask that you please come forward," Pickett said. "It may seem like it's nothing, it may seem insignificant, please send it in."This story will be updated when more information becomes available.

title: Tom Fornelli's CFP Vibe Check: Ohio State switches to survival mode in fight to make College Football Playoff - CBS Sports

body:
Every week the CFP Vibe Check tries to put its finger on where things stand in the College Football Playoff race without overreacting to what it just saw, but also probably overreacting to everything it just saw. In the not-so-long history of the College Football Playoff, there are only two teams that have managed to finish ranked in the final CFP ranking each season: Ohio State and Alabama. What's even more impressive for the Buckeyes is that they've never finished a season ranked lower than No. 7.That means if there had been a 12-team field since the inception of the CFP, Ohio State would've made it every year. Even Alabama would've missed out in 2019.Yet, here we are, in the third season of the actual 12-team field, and there's a very real shot No. 2 Ohio State won't be in it. The Buckeyes lost to USC 30-18 Saturday night, continuing the 2026 season's theme of top teams losing to unranked teams. However, this loss probably shouldn't have been all that much of a shock.
Even if the Buckeyes were favored by a touchdown, they were still on the road with a first-time starter at QB, and a true freshman at that. And while USC may be perennially disappointing, there's quite a difference between a disappointing USC and a disappointing Rutgers. The Trojans have five-star recruits too.Luke Fahey, the freshman in question, looked every bit the part. He overthrew open passes and learned that, no matter what seemingly everybody outside the program thought, it's not as easy as just "throw it to Jeremiah Smith." He panicked when pressured, and sometimes even only when he thought he was being pressured. There were presnap penalties that often accompany new QBs.And there weren't nearly enough points on the scoreboard.It was one of the uglier Ohio State performances of recent memory, and it's the second loss of the season, which drastically thins this team's margin of error going forward. I expect Fahey to improve the more he plays, but I don't know that he'll improve enough. Next week the Buckeyes will be back at home facing an Oregon team that suddenly looked like it got its act together in a 34-26 win over No. 20 Northwestern. Dylan Raiola threw for 336 yards and 3 touchdowns, and the explosive plays that had been lacking for most of the year returned.
I don't know if Ohio State can get past the version of Oregon I saw Saturday. Even if they do, I don't know that the version of Ohio State we saw can get past Northwestern, Nebraska and Michigan. Make no mistake about it: while the 19-15 win over Indiana is one of the better wins any team will be able to claim this season, the rest of the resume is looking a bit thin right now.If the Buckeyes lose to Oregon and win out, would a 9-3 record with wins over Indiana and Iowa be enough to get in over other 9-3 SEC teams? Or if the Buckeyes beat Oregon, but drop one of those other three games, how much is the Oregon win worth? The Ducks would be an 8-4 team at best.This is a brand new position for Ohio State in the playoff era. There will be a level of tension throughout Columbus in November that's never been felt before.
What about USC?First of all, what an incredible outcome for Lincoln Riley's supporters and his haters. His supporters got a top-five win to crow about, and his haters got a top-five win with a giant asterisk on it since it was against a team without its starting quarterback.While they argue with one another, there's no debate that this win does a lot for USC's playoff case. At DraftKings, USC's odds of making the playoff increased from +1900 (5%) pregame to +300 (25%) after the win. But I'm not a believer in this team's hopes going forward. The win is great, but after a bye this weekend, the Trojans will be on the road to face No. 4 Indiana. The last time they went on the road, they lost 24-7 to Wisconsin. The same Wisconsin that lost 30-0 to Iowa on Saturday. They also have a date with still-undefeated UCLA at the Rose Bowl to finish the regular season.
You'll have to forgive me for not thinking that a win over an Ohio State team without Julian Sayin means the Trojans are about to run the table. With that 17-point loss to Wisconsin, I cannot see this USC team getting in at 9-3, and what if Ohio State collapses down the stretch? Suddenly that win looks pretty hollow in the eyes of the committee.You did get that top-five win, though. Nobody can take that from you.Respect Wake Forest
I know that, ultimately, every College Football Playoff ranking that's released before the final one is meaningless. However, the one aspect I appreciate about the meaningless rankings is that they give us a glimpse of what the committee thinks, and that's probably more valuable in a season like this one than it's been in previous seasons.And I can't wait to see what the committee thinks of No. 14 Wake Forest. My instinct is that the Deacons will not be ranked inside the top 12 on Tuesday night. They play in the wrong conference, have the wrong logo on their helmet, and they don't have a signature win. The highlight of their resume is probably not getting killed by Miami in a 33-20 loss back in September.
But I kinda think this team is pretty good. Their schedule, compared to other contenders, is not very strong. However, the Demon Deacons are treating inferior competition the way you want to see a good team do so. After Saturday's 51-7 victory vs. Virginia on Saturday, they've won their last four games against Stanford, NC State, Cal and the Cavaliers by a combined score of 187-31. I know how you're reacting to that. "Who cares? Those teams stink."You're right, they do, but look around. Tell me how many other teams you've seen this season consistently dominate the teams that stink on their schedule. In a season in which it's made clearer every week that there isn't a truly dominant team, perhaps we should show some respect to one of the few teams that is dominating their opponents.Miami isn't untouchable
The good news for No. 1 Miami is that it beat North Carolina 38-35 to improve to 8-0 on the season. The win moved Miami's odds to make the CFP at DraftKings from -3300 (97.1%) to -6000 (98.4%), tying them with Georgia for the best odds in the country. Basically, they're telling you that, even with a loss to Notre Dame next week, Miami's still highly likely to win the ACC and make the College Football Playoff.
That's all great news! The problem is, did you see the score I mentioned above? Yeah, Miami only beat North Carolina by three points, and it actually trailed at times in both the third and fourth quarters. North Carolina's Billy Edwards threw for 341 yards and four touchdowns. This was a couple of weeks after Florida State's Ashton Daniels threw for four touchdowns against the Canes as well.The Miami team that dominated early this year has begun to show some vulnerabilities on defense. The kind that could certainly impact them against Notre Dame next week, and in the College Football Playoff in the highly likely event the Canes make the field.Of course, even with the defensive question marks, Miami still has Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney, and sometimes the best defense is a good offense. Still, it's worth monitoring going forward because while a loss to No. 5 Notre Dame alone won't keep the Canes out, it could have an impact on their seeding.
The Big 12 dust is settling
While the dreams of three-bigs in the Big 12 died last week with Texas Tech's loss at Cincinnati, the league's overall picture has become clearer, and it's basically the picture we all expected to see. No. 6 Utah shoved Houston out of it last week, and No. 13 Texas Tech responded to its loss by pushing Arizona out of the picture this week with a 34-26 victory. In Ames, Iowa State pretended it was 2011 all over again and ended Oklahoma State's already slim playoff hopes too by defeating the Cowboys 51-49.Tech may have also found an identity in the process. Thomas Castellanos started at QB over Will Hammond, and he gave you a Thomas Castellanos performance. He hit a few big plays in the passing game while being pretty inaccurate, and used his legs to great effect. I don't know if it's the kind of formula that can lead Texas Tech on a playoff run, but it's the kind that could at least get the Red Raiders back to the playoff.Utah obliterated Cincinnati 49-25 in a game that was 42-6 at halftime to keep the Utes undefeated. As a result, they're the only Big 12 team with implied odds of better than 50% of making the CFP field (they're at 70.6%. Utah could put a stranglehold on a Big 12 Championship Game appearance with a win next week against BYU.
Speaking of BYU, I'm not sure what happened Saturday in its 27-20 victory vs. Arizona State. Perhaps the Cougars completely closed up shop at halftime and started to prepare for Utah, but letting a zombified Arizona State team battle back from a 17-3 deficit to tie the game at 17-17 late in the third quarter wasn't a great look. This team has not looked nearly as good as the team that beat Notre Dame in its two games since, and next week is probably a must-win for the Cougars.The G6 race might get weird
If you didn't stay up until the wee hours of the morning to watch No. 29 Boise State's 46-45 win over Texas State, shame on you. You'll have to figure out a way to live with yourself, because this game went off the rails.Boise State had a 28-3 lead at halftime, and that lead evaporated stunningly fast. Texas State reeled off 36 unanswered in the first 23 minutes of the second half to take a 39-28 lead. Then Boise State QB Maddux Madsen left the game with an injury, and in came somebody named Max Cutforth who had to save Boise State's season.
And he did.Max Cutforth put forth a heroic effort, throwing for 131 yards and 3 touchdowns in a quarter and a half! Boise State somehow won 46-45 to maintain control of the Pac-12 race. Oregon State's loss to Fresno State only improved matters for the Broncos.But we don't know the extent of Madsen's injury, or how it could impact Boise State going forward. The Broncos still must play Oregon State and could face the Beavers again in the Pac-12 Championship. I don't know how the committee would view a two-loss Boise State team, especially if there are one-loss teams from the other leagues.The Broncos still have the best odds of making the field at DraftKings among G6 teams, but New Mexico, UTSA, and even Liberty all closed the gap considerably this week. Rest In CFPeaceEach week for the rest of the season we shall recognize the schools who saw their playoff hopes die over the weekendAuburnCincinnatiJames MadisonMinnesotaNebraskaNorth CarolinaOklahomaOklahoma StateOregon StateUCFWisconsinWeek 10 Vibe ShiftersA look ahead to the five games on next week's slate most likely to impact the playoff raceNo. 1 Miami at No. 5 Notre DameNo. 8 BYU at No. 6 UtahNo. 10 Alabama at No. 15 LSUNo. 3 Georgia at No. 12 Ole MissOregon at No. 2 Ohio StateThis week's CFP ProjectionThis is a projection of what I expect the top 12 to be Tuesday nightMiamiGeorgiaNotre DameIndianaUtahUCLABYUKentuckyAlabamaTexasOhio StateOle MissBoise State will be the highest ranked G6 school.

title: Dream star Angel Reese vows 'we'll be back' after Game 7 loss vs. Valkyries in WNBA Finals - CBS Sports
description: Reese was limited to eight points on Saturday night as Atlanta fell short of a title against Golden State
body:
Reese was limited to eight points on Saturday night as Atlanta fell short of a title against Golden State
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 1, 2026
                            
                    at
    12:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Angel Reese was, understandably, devastated as her third WNBA season came to a close on Saturday night in a Game 7 loss in the WNBA Finals to the Golden State Valkyries, 68-63. But even with the heartache, the Dream forward -- who was traded from the Chicago Sky to Atlanta in April -- expressed appreciation for the Dream organization and her teammates for the best season of her young WNBA career."They changed my life, and I'm just so grateful for them, and I'm so thankful for them," she said. "And it is tough in the moment, but we'll be back. And I always say delayed, not denied, and this is only Year 3."Reese was named Defensive Player of the Year this season, made her third All-Star team and was named to the All-WNBA second team as well, which makes her eligible for the EPIC extension. She set the single-season rebounding record, single-season double-double record and single-game rebounding record. Her offensive game improved drastically under the guidance of Dream coach Karl Smesko, who worked directly with Reese to re-make her shot.But she struggled in Game 7, with just eight points. She shot 3 of 7 from the field (42.9%), 1 of 3 from outside (33.3%) and 1 of 3 from the line (33.3%). Reese had 12 rebounds -- nine offensive, three defensive -- as well as one assist, one steal and two blocks, but her four turnovers were very costly. She had zero shot attempts in the fourth quarter and only got to the line once in the final frame. It was a performance that will likely haunt her in the offseason, but she kept things in perspective after the game.
"I'm really proud of the year that I had. I mean, I've done a lot of great things this year, but I wouldn't be able to do it without this group," Reese said. "We've won a lot of great games, and to come all the way to the Finals with this group, I mean, it says a lot. Not a lot of people have this opportunity to do it. And, like I said, I'd do it all over again with this same group, just battling with them every single day, I love these girls. I love the coaches. I think it also sucks because our fan base back home poured into us so much this year, and we really wanted to do it for them. But we're forever grateful, and like I said, we'll be back."
        
            
                'I stayed patient': How Finals MVP Gabby Williams made history in Game 7 to fuel Valkyries to WNBA title
                
                    Jack Maloney                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
In the series, Reese averaged 14.7 points and 12.6 rebounds per game. In Game 2, she had a record-setting 30-point, 16-rebound showing, and followed that up with 21 points and 12 rebounds in Game 4. She had four double-doubles in the series. However, she was held to eight or fewer points in three of the Dream's four losses.She is looking forward to a full offseason working with Smesko and better learning the Dream's system, and knows that her first playoff run will help her grow in the long run. After a couple of years in Chicago that were filled with off-court change and roster turnover, she has finally found stability and success in Atlanta.
"Honestly, I really enjoy just being around a group of girls that just come to work every day and want to work and want to get better, and they push me to be better," she said. "I'm a young player and I'm very vocal, but I think they really help me mature in different ways that I haven't really been challenged."

body:
Oddsmsakers have dropped the opening lines for a loaded Week 10 slate

        With Week 9 in the books, can we all admit that everyone was looking ahead to Week 10 just a little bit? That's because this weekend features one of the most highly-anticipated slate of games with one marquee matchup after another all day, and the oddsmakers have dropped opening lines for each game.No. 15 LSU and No. 10 Alabama meet in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, in what could be a College Football Playoff elimination game. The Crimson Tide have owned the Tigers in Death Valley recently, but Keelon Russell struggled mightily in his last game. Despite that home-field advantage, LSU is only a slight favorite as both teams look to avoid a third loss.The primetime matchup with No. 5 Notre Dame hosting top-ranked Miami is one of the top games of the season. Both teams have shown some vulnerability lately with the Fighting Irish losing to BYU and the Hurricanes narrowly escaping Florida State and North Carolina. Notre Dame opened as a small 4.5-point favorite, at least in part due to the setting, but also because the Miami secondary just got exposed by the Tar Heels in its 38-35 victory Saturday.Elsewhere on a loaded slate, No. 2 Ohio State is a two-score favorite against Oregon, No. 6 Utah is favored over No. 8 BYU in the Holy War and No. 12 Ole Miss is a home underdog against No. 3 Georgia. Check out the opening lines for all of Week 10's biggest games below.
The big gamesNo. 8 BYU at No. 6 Utah (-4.5): Set your alarms because the Holy War kicks off at 10 a.m. local time this year. This matchup is one of the most highly-anticipated ever with both teams eying a Big 12 championship and a spot in the College Football Playoff. BYU hasn't been at its best since beating Notre Dame a few weeks ago, and Utah has only gotten stronger. That may not bode well for the Cougars, but they also own a three-game winning streak in this series, and we saw that they were capable of at their peak against the Fighting Irish.No. 11 Texas (-3.5) at No. 23 Missouri: Have the Longhorns finally started to hit their stride? They've conquered the state of Mississippi over the last couple weeks, but a different kind of test awaits Saturday. Texas will take its show on the road to Columbia where it will face a dangerous Missouri team. The Tigers have an explosive passing game led by quarterback Austin Simmons, but their running game just got reinforced as Ahmad Hardy has returned from a gunshot wound he suffered in the offseason. If Colin Simmons remains sidelined for Texas, that will put more pressure on Arch Manning and the offense.Oregon at No. 2 Ohio State (-10.5): Oregon is coming off a top-25 win over Northwestern, and Ohio State suffered a devastating loss to USC on Saturday. Despite that, the Vegas oddsmakers still see the Buckeyes as a clear favorite against the Ducks. Ohio State will likely start freshman quarterback Luke Fahey, but it's not like Oregon's quarterback situation is ideal either. Although he has more experience, Dylan Raiola has been prone to extreme highs and lows. The Ohio State defense has enough talent to get pressure on Raiola, and he tends to make mistakes when that happens.
No. 10 Alabama at No. 15 LSU (-3.5): Would this line be bigger if it were a night kickoff as Lane Kiffin wished? I guess we'll never know, but Tiger Stadium hasn't exactly been a safe place for LSU against Alabama recently. The Tigers are 1-6 in their last seven home games against the Crimson Tide. On the other hand, the last time we saw sophomore Keelon Russell on the road, he was struggling against Tennessee. The atmosphere won't be any friendlier in Baton Rouge. Could this game serve as a College Football Playoff eliminator? It's hard to rule anything out in a chaotic college football season, but the loser will be in jeopardy of missing out for sure.No. 9 Kentucky at No. 16 Tennessee (-6.5): Will Stein has Big Blue Nation believing Kentucky can reach the College Football Playoff as the calendar flips to November. And why not? The Wildcats have passed almost every test they've faced to this point, although a night game in Neyland Stadium is one of the toughest challenges left on the schedule. Tennessee's defense has proven that it's playoff-caliber, but the offense has work to do. It'll be interesting to see how young quarterback George MacIntyre responds after two disastrous plays in the final few minutes against South Carolina.No. 1 Miami at No. 5 Notre Dame (-4.5): On a slate full of marquee games, this stands out as the biggest. Even though it already has a loss to BYU on its schedule, Notre Dame is probably still in the playoff if it loses, but the margin for error would be zero with a loss to the Hurricanes. Perhaps it was a look-ahead spot, but the Hurricanes defense looked particularly vulnerable in Saturday's 38-35 win over North Carolina. If Billy Edwards Jr. can throw for 341 yards against the Miami secondary, it's probably safe to assume there will be holes that CJ Carr can exploit. That is part of the reason Notre Dame is a narrow favorite.
No. 3 Georgia (-3.5) at No. 12 Ole Miss: This one would likely be a playoff eliminator for Ole Miss. Its win vs. Louisville has lost a lot of shine, and the Rebels don't have any opportunities for quality wins the rest of the way. The good news for Ole Miss is that Trinidad Chambliss gives the team a real shot to pull the upset at home. Despite a lopsided 27-8 win vs. Florida on Saturday, the Georgia passing attack was ineffective against one of the worst secondaries in the SEC. If the Rebels can score and force the Bulldogs to open up their passing attack, things could get very interesting in Oxford.Best of the restVirginia Tech at No. 19 SMU (-6.5)Michigan State at Michigan (-13.5)No. 7 UCLA (-5.5) at MinnesotaTexas A&M at South Carolina (-6.5)Penn State at Washington (-1.5)Cincinnati at No. 18 Houston (-10.5)Iowa at No. 20 Northwestern (-1.5)Oklahoma at Florida (-6.5)

The Bills have given up 29 or more points in every game but one this season, and Jackson is a top-six QB in his return, even though we have some concern about whether he will run as much as he typically does. His return puts Zay Flowers inside the top five at receiver and boosts Derrick Henry back inside the top 12 despite some uninspiring efficiency this season.Here's what else we're monitoring:UPDATE: Moore expected to playD.J. Moore is expected to make his return to the Bills lineup and is worth firing up in almost any format in what could turn into a high-scoring affair against the Ravnes. Emeka Egbuka is outEgbuka was able to progress through the concussion protocol but still missed practice Friday and will not play in Week 8. This puts Chris Godwin in play as a high-floor WR3 against the Falcons and should be plenty of targets for Bucky Irving. We don't really want to start anyone else for Tampa Bay, though Ted Hurts could be a decent dart throw as a flex.Saquon Barkley will try to play, but team remains beat upSaquon Barkley returned to practice on Friday and has said he will try to play on Sunday. We are not expecting him to be his old self, but he is still, just barely, an RB2. Barkley turned 9 touches into 15 last week, but the Commanders run defense is a tougher matchup than the Cowboys. Devonta Smith, and Dontayvion Wicks missed practice on Friday and we are not expecting them to play. This makes Makai Lemon a good option as a WR3 and Dallas Goedert a must-start at tight end.
A.J. Brown misses Friday practice, projected outBrown missed practice on Thursday and Friday after a limited session on Wednesday, putting his Week 8 status in doubt. He is listed as questionable, but we have pulled him from the rankings and have some concern for his rest-of-season value. Demario Douglas is our favorite Patriots wide receiver and he is a high-end WR3. Kyle Williams and Efton Chism are both dart throws as flexes.  Hunter Henry and Drake Maye are the only sure starters on this team, and Rhamondre Stevenson is a low-end RB2 in a great matchup. TreVeyon Henderson also missed practice on Friday with an illness, which could make Stevenson a better play.Tyler Warren cleared to playThis is a much-needed return for the Colts and Fantasy managers alike. Warren moves right back into the top five at tight end and should be viewed as a must-start tight end. He hasn't had much impact on Josh Downs' targets but he does knock Keenan Allen down a notch, because they are both working in the same area of the field. Allen is still a WR3 in full PPR, but we aren't as excited about him as we were at the beginning of the week.Jeremiyah Love is backThere may still be a small window open to buy low on Love, who has immense upside if he's healthy enough to handle a larger role. For now, we are projecting Love for 12 touches this week, which makes him a fine flex. Tyler Allgeier has a similar projection and is ranked slightly lower. Hopefully Zononvan Knight's performance doesn't turn this backfield into a three-headed monster.
Tyjae Spears and Carnell Tate both miss practice on FridayWe aren't expecting either Spears or Tate to play in Week 8. Spears didn't play last week, and it looks likely we will get another week of Tony Pollard as a workhorse. View him as a solid RB2, assuming he doesn't get traded before Sunday. Wan'Dale Robinson should be the big target winner with Tate out, and profiles as a high-end WR3 in full PPR. He is less valuable in half- and non-PPR leagues.Ladd McConkey working way through concussion protocolMcConkey got a full practice in on Thursday, so he should be good to go. This is not a very good matchup against the Rams, and the Chargers have been a disaster offensively, so we wouldn't view McConkey as more than a WR3. We would prefer to sit all Chargers against the Rams this week.DJ Moore in non-contact jersey for second day in a rowThis is a big one, and we don't have much clarity on it yet. Moore is dealing with a shoulder injury, and it is a positive that he is practicing, but the uncertainty remains because he has not yet been cleared for contact. If he plays, we will view him as a WR2 with upside in a shootout against the Ravens. If Moore is out, then Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir are attractive WR3 options, though Coleman would be our favorite. Moore isn't the only Bills pass catcher who is questionable; Dalton Kincaid also has a chest injury. We are expecting Kincaid to play, but be sure to check again on Sunday morning.

Unfortunately, he's facing the Denver Broncos, who are also expected to get Patrick Surtain back. Rice's return is a big hit to Xavier Worthy, who is a WR3 without Rice and a low-end flex with Rice. Travis Kelce also takes a bit of a hit, but he remains a top 12 tight end. View Rice as a WR3 in a very tough matchup and just hope he gets through the week without further injury.Jadarian Price has his practice window openedGood grief. The Seahawks may have both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price back in Week 8. Honestly, no one has any reason to have any confidence in who would lead this backfield in touches. The only thing we feel confident in is that Emanuel Wilson is no longer a good RB2 for Fantasy purposes. No Seahawks back should be viewed as more than a flex in Week 8.Breece Hall limited again, will be questionableThis is a big one. If Hall is out again, then Braelon Allen remains a must-start running back. If Hall is back, then we are splitting the baby and viewing both Allen and Hall as borderline RB2s. What would make the most sense is if Allen led on rushing downs with a 60-40 split and Hall played the majority of passing downs. The Colts need to replenish their draft assets, and dealing their three-time Pro Bowl running back could produce a significant return

        After a loss to the previously winless Titans dropped the Colts to 2-4 on the young season, Indianapolis fired GM Chris Ballard. It was the first firing by Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon, and it might not be the last. Shane Steichen has zero postseason trips in four seasons as the Colts' coach, and while he's still leading the way for now, there's no doubt his seat is and has been warm. How much warmer it became after Ballard's firing is unclear, but it's clear Irsay-Gordon expects better than what the Colts are producing.It's also clear that the Colts aren't close to getting to the level Irsay-Gordon expects. Daniel Jones has been a turnover machine, and the defense is below average, with issues rushing the passer and defending the run. The Colts are 28th in yards per play allowed and 26th in net yards per attempt allowed.Sometimes it has to get worse before it gets better, and that may be the case for the Colts. Indianapolis is already down a 2027 first-round pick, traded to the Jets at the 2025 trade deadline, but the Colts could be sellers -- and maybe major sellers -- this year.The biggest name would be star running back Jonathan Taylor. He had 20 touchdowns and nearly 2,000 yards from scrimmage last year, and he's on his way to another big season, but the Colts are stuck going nowhere once again. He's 27 and has played in just one playoff game -- as a rookie in 2020. In fact, Taylor headlined Jordan Dajani's list of five players we want to see moved by the Nov. 10 deadline.

        
            
                NFL trade deadline: 5 players we'd like to see get a change of scenery, including Jonathan Taylor
                
                    Jordan Dajani                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Taylor would have plenty of suitors if made available, and the situation isn't too dissimilar from what the Panthers were going through with Christian McCaffrey in 2022. McCaffrey is a more versatile player than Taylor in the passing game and was younger than Taylor is now when that deal happened, but he had also been injured. In the deal with the 49ers in 2022, Carolina received second-, third-, fourth- and fifth-round picks.With that in mind, here are five teams who could come calling about Taylor and what a mock trade might look like:
                            
    
                                                
                    
    New York GiantsGiants receive: RB Jonathan TaylorColts receive: RB Cam Skattebo, 2027 second-round pick, 2028 fourth-round pick
The Giants used a four-running-back committee Sunday against the Saints and then released Najee Harris (who didn't exactly love the rotation). In between, John Harbaugh explained his rationale, saying he "would love" to have a "Derrick Henry circumstance or a 'Saquon Barkley circumstance." Whether he meant to or not, it was surely a bummer for Giants fans to hear Harbaugh mention his running back from last year and a former Giants running back in the same sentence. Regardless, Taylor could be that type of workhorse. The Colts getting two high draft picks over the next two years, plus Skattebo, who showed promise as a rookie but didn't have a single touch Sunday, on a cost-effective deal, would be a solid start. The Giants are leading a historically bad NFC East, and even if it doesn't finish that way, having Taylor next to Jaxson Dart next year would be an enticing prospect.One thing to note, though, is that Harbaugh comes from one of the most patient, draft-and-develop franchises in Baltimore. This would be a significant departure from that.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Cincinnati BengalsBengals receive: RB Jonathan Taylor, 2027 fourth-round pickColts receive: RB Chase Brown, 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick
This would be similar to the package the Panthers got for McCaffrey, but instead of a third-round pick, the Colts would get Brown. At 26, he's younger and has less wear and tear than Taylor. He's also an accomplished player and productive pass catcher who has handled a bell-cow workload before. A change of scenery could do him good, as he has struggled to get going early this season. For the Bengals, this would be a second major win-now move in just over six months; they sent the No. 10 pick to the Giants in April for Dexter Lawrence. The Bengals have tried to work in more under-center looks, but are among the worst teams using it. Taylor could change that single-handedly. Cincinnati also has an extra third-round pick, which helps make giving up so many picks easier to swallow.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Denver BroncosBroncos receive: RB Jonathan Taylor, 2027 fifth-round pickColts receive: RB J.K. Dobbins, 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fourth-round pickThe Broncos traded a first-round pick for an upgrade at wide receiver in Jaylen Waddle this offseason (though it hasn't really worked out yet). Would they make another big deal for an upgrade at running back in Taylor? The Broncos have struggled to muster much on the ground, exacerbating quarterback Bo Nix's struggles. Dobbins is on a two-year deal, though there's an out after this year should the Colts choose to use it.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Seattle SeahawksSeahawks receive: RB Jonathan TaylorColts receive: RB Jadarian Price, 2027 second-round pickIt'd be rare to see a team move on from a first-round pick so quickly, but the Seahawks are in a rare position as the first team to lose a Super Bowl MVP in over two decades. Seattle very much misses Kenneth Walker III and is struggling to find much of anything on the ground without him. Price is on IR, and Emanuel Wilson and George Holani have had devastating fumbles. Offensive coordinator Brian Fleury has been with the 49ers since 2019, so he knows the value of a great top running back. Indianapolis would get a good young running back and ample future picks.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota VikingsVikings receive: RB Jonathan TaylorColts receive: RB Jordan Mason, 2027 second-round pick, 2027 fifth-round pick
The 5-0 Vikings have shown signs of an improved run game this year, and Mason is on his way back from a thumb injury that had him on IR, but Taylor would be a game-changer, and combining him with a mobile quarterback in Kyler Murray would be a treat for Kevin O'Connell. Mason, meanwhile, is a good player on his own accord. Plus, the Vikings have draft capital to spare, with an extra third, two extra fifths and two extra sixths.

Sweat has two sacks on the season entering Week 8

        As the NFL approaches the Nov. 10 trade deadline, names of players who could be on the move are starting to percolate. That includes Arizona Cardinals pass rusher Josh Sweat, who ESPN reports is garnering trade interest across the league. At 2-5 coming into Week 8 and sitting in last place in the NFC West, Arizona is eyed as a potential seller at the deadline. Already, the team traded former first-round wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans, and it's possible that Sweat could be the next veteran who is shipped out of town for future draft capital. The 29-year-old signed a four-year, $76.4 million contract with the Cardinals back in 2025 during free agency. While he is signed through 2028, Sweat has no guaranteed salary after the 2026 campaign, per Over The Cap. Before inking that deal with Arizona, Sweat spent the first seven years of his career with the Philadelphia Eagles, who drafted him in the fourth round of the 2018 NFL Draft out of Florida State. He was named to the Pro Bowl in 2021 and helped Philly win Super Bowl LIX during his final season with the franchise. In that championship win over Kansas City, Sweat tallied 2.5 sacks. 
During his first season with Arizona in 2025, Sweat recorded a career-high 12 sacks to go along with 17 quarterback hits. Through seven games played this season, the veteran has two sacks, four quarterback hits, and three tackles for loss. Sweat's future with the Cardinals had been murky even before this looming trade deadline. He reportedly asked for a trade in the aftermath of head coach Jonathan Gannon -- who coached him as the defensive coordinator in Philadelphia -- being fired last offseason. However, the front office denied the request at the time.Has that sentiment from the organization changed now that they're circling a last-place finish in 2026? Teams are apparently inquiring about that possibility by seeing if the pass rusher is available.
Josh Sweat landing spots
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Dallas CowboysAlongside ESPN's report noting interest in Sweat, there was a note that the Cowboys are among the teams to watch in this race. Jerry Jones has been extremely active over the last calendar year as he tries to improve his defense, most recently striking a trade with the Pittsburgh Steelers for corner Joey Porter Jr. Now, they could be doubling down and adding a pass rusher like Sweat to help a defense that is still struggling. Entering Week 8, Dallas is tied for the third-most total yards per game allowed (373.7) and the second-most rushing yards per game allowed (145.7). The defense is also last in opponent third-down conversion rate (52.%) and 30th in takeaways (4). When it comes to getting after the quarterback, the Cowboys are tied for the fourth-fewest sacks in the league and are bottom-10 in the NFL in pressures. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Green Bay PackersGreen Bay doesn't necessarily have the same need for a pass rusher as some other clubs in the NFL, as they boast Lukas Van Ness off the edge and are set to get back star edge Micah Parsons in the near future as well. They have a 7.2% sack rate, which just cracks the top-10 in the NFL, while owning a 36.1% pressure rate that is middle of the pack. 
The big reason why this could be a landing spot for Sweat is simply due to the presence of Jonathan Gannon, who is the current defensive coordinator in Green Bay. Gannon coached Sweat as the DC in Philadelphia and then followed him to Arizona as a free agent after he was hired as the head coach. That rapport could embolden the Packers to reunite this duo and add to what is already a growing strength with Parsons' looming return. After Chicago made a blockbuster move for Jeffery Simmons earlier this week, Green Bay could look to join the arms race. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Buffalo BillsThe Buffalo Bills are firmly in a Super Bowl window with Josh Allen playing at the peak of his powers. Entering Week 8, the Bills QB leads the NFL in total touchdowns (17) and has Buffalo sitting atop the AFC East at 5-1. The one thing that may hold the franchise back from finally getting over the hump, however, is the defense. This season, the Bills defense ranks 30th in points allowed per game (28.5), 27th on third down (45%), 31st in penalties per game (3.7), and last in points allowed per drive (2.76). When it comes to the pass rush, the Bills are 20th in pressure rate and 27th in sack rate. Sweat could come in and immediately give them a presence off the edge as someone with a double-digit sack ceiling. Once the playoff push begins, attacking the quarterback will become paramount, making this type of move necessary for Buffalo.
